content.title: Spurs vs. Warriors: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (4/1/26)
content.text: The San Antonio Spurs (57–18) face the Golden State Warriors (36–39) tonight at Chase Center in San Francisco. The Spurs are red hot, riding a nine-game winning streak. But they’ve been unable to gain ground on the first-place Oklahoma City Thunder, who have been just as strong, with both teams winning nine of their last 10 games. San Antonio trails OKC by 2.5 games for the top spot in the Western Conference with seven games remaining in the regular season. While they remain mathematically in the race for the No. 1 seed, the second seed appears more likely. San Antonio is coming off a 129–114 win over the Chicago Bulls on Monday night, powered by a dominant performance from Victor Wembanyama, who posted 41 points and 16 rebounds. He reached 10 points and 10 boards in under nine minutes. Stephon Castle added 21 points and 10 assists, falling just two rebounds short of a triple-double. The Spurs shot 51% from the field. Golden State, meanwhile, enters after a 116–93 loss to the Denver Nuggets, snapping a three-game winning streak that came against some of the league’s lower-tier teams. Kristaps Porzingis and Brandin Podziemski led the Warriors with 23 points apiece, each shooting 8-of-14 from the field and hitting five three-pointers. But they struggled to keep pace with a high-efficiency Nuggets offense. The Warriors, however, should get a boost soon, with Stephen Curry expected to return this weekend when they face the Houston Rockets — just in time as Golden State closes out the regular season and heads into the play-in tournament. Porzingis and Podziemski could help keep this game close early on, but expect the Spurs to separate in the second half for a comfortable double-digit win. Final Score Prediction: San Antonio Spurs 121, Golden State Warriors 104 Injury Report San Antonio Spurs David Jones-Garcia — OFS (Ankle) Golden State Warriors Quinten Post — Day-To-Day (Foot) Will Richard — Day-To-Day (Heel) Stephen Curry — Out (Knee) Al Horford — Out (Calf) Moses Moody — Out (Knee) Jimmy Butler III — Out (Knee) How to Watch Spurs vs. Warriors Tip-off for tonight’s Spurs-Warriors game is set for 10:00 PM Eastern / 7:00 PM Pacific at Chase Center in San Francisco. The game airs live nationally on ESPN and streams on the ESPN app and website. If you’re a cord-cutter without an active livestreaming plan, you can watch the game for free by taking advantage of free trials from DIRECTV STREAM, Hulu + Live TV, Fubo TV, or YouTube TV. Fubo TV and Hulu + Live TV include ESPN Unlimited as part of their standard plans.
